Let $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ be squares inside $ABC$ with disjoint interiors such that they both have one side lying on $AB$. The two squares each have an edge lying on a common line perpendicular to $AB$, and $\mathcal{P}$ has one vertex on $AC$ while $\mathcal{Q}$ has one vertex on $AB$. Determine the minimum value of the sum of the areas of the two squares.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 5$, $BC = 4$ and $AC = 3$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ be squares inside $ABC$ with disjoint interiors such that they both have one side lying on $AB$. The two squares each have an edge lying on a common line perpendicular to $AB$, and $\mathcal{P}$ has one vertex on $BC$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ has one vertex on $AC$. Determine the minimum value of the sum of the areas of the two squares.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 5$, $BC = 4$ and $AC = 3$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ be squares inside $ABC$ with disjoint interiors such that they both have one side lying on $AB$. The two squares each have an edge lying on a common line parallel to $AB$, and $\mathcal{P}$ has one vertex on $AC$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ has one vertex on $BC$. Determine the minimum value of the sum of the areas of the two squares.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Place a point $P$ on segment $AC$ such that the ratio $AP : PC = 2 : 1$. If $BP = 1$, find the largest possible area of triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text: Suppose that $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $P$ be the point on side $AC$ so that $AP = 2CP$. Given that $BP = 1$, determine the maximum possible perimeter of $ABC$.
Suppose that $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $P$ be the point on side $AC$ so that $AP = 2CP$. Given that $BP = 1$, determine the minimum possible area of $ABC$.
Suppose that $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $P$ be the point on side $AC$ so that $AP = 2CP$. Given that $BP = 2$, determine the maximum possible area of $ABC$.

positive_text:
Let $(a, b)$ be a pair of real numbers satisfying
$$
56 a + 33 b = \frac{-b}{a^{2} + b^{2}}, \quad \text{ and } \quad 33 a - 56 b = \frac{a}{a^{2} + b^{2}}
$$
Determine the value of $|a| + |b|$.

negatives.text:
Let $(x, y)$ be a pair of real numbers satisfying
$$
56 x + 33 y = \frac{y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}, \quad \text{ and } \quad 33 x - 56 y = \frac{x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}
$$
Determine the value of $|x| + |y|$.

Let $(x, y)$ be a pair of real numbers satisfying
$$
56 x + 33 y = \frac{-y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}, \quad \text{ and } \quad 33 x + 56 y = \frac{x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}
$$
Determine the value of $|x| + |y|$.

Let $(x, y)$ be a pair of real numbers satisfying
$$
56 x + 33 y = \frac{-y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}, \quad \text{ and } \quad 33 x - 56 y = \frac{x^{2}}{x^{2} + y^{2}}
$$
Determine the value of $|x| + |y|$.

positive_text: \text{a. Find four distinct positive integers } a, b, c, d \text{ such that } \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} + \frac{1}{d} = 1.\\\text{b. Find five distinct positive integers } a, b, c, d, e \text{ such that } \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} + \frac{1}{d} + \frac{1}{e} = 1.\\\text{c. Prove that, for any integer } n > 3, 1 \text{ can be written as a sum of } n \text{ distinct unit fractions.}

negatives.text: \text{a. Write } 1 \text{ as a sum of } 4 \text{ distinct unit fractions where each denominator is odd.}\\\text{b. Write } 1 \text{ as a sum of } 5 \text{ distinct unit fractions where each denominator is odd.}\\\text{c. Show that, for any integer } k > 3, 1 \text{ can be decomposed into } k \text{ unit fractions with odd denominators.}

\text{a. Write } 1 \text{ as a sum of } 4 \text{ distinct unit squares.}\\\text{b. Write } 1 \text{ as a sum of } 5 \text{ distinct unit squares.}\\\text{c. Show that, for any integer } k > 3, 1 \text{ can be decomposed into } k \text{ unit squares.}

\text{a. Write } 2 \text{ as a sum of } 4 \text{ distinct unit fractions.}\\\text{b. Write } 2 \text{ as a sum of } 5 \text{ distinct unit fractions.}\\\text{c. Show that, for any integer } k > 3, 2 \text{ can be decomposed into } k \text{ unit fractions.}

positive_text: Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are positive real numbers with $x^{y} > y^{x}$ and $y^{z} > z^{y}$. Is it necessarily true that $x^{z} > z^{x}$?

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be positive real numbers with $a^{b} > b^{a}$ and $b^{c} > c^{b}$. Does it follow that $a^{c} < c^{a}$?
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be positive real numbers with $a^{b} > b^{a}$ and $b^{c} > c^{b}$. Does it follow that $a^{c} = c^{a}$?

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be right-angled at $A$, and let a circle be tangent to $AB$ and $AC$ at $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Suppose the points opposite $X$ and $Y$ on the circle lie on segment $BC$. If $AB = 6$, compute the area of the region of the circle that lies outside triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, and let a circle be tangent to $AB$ and $AC$ at $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Suppose the points diametrically opposite $X$ and $Y$ lie on the extension of $BC$ beyond $C$. Given $AB = 6$, find the area of the portion of the circle outside the triangle.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, and let a circle be tangent to $AB$ and $AC$ at $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Suppose the points diametrically opposite $X$ and $Y$ both lie on segment $AB$. Given $AB = 6$, find the area of the portion of the circle outside the triangle.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, and let a circle be tangent to $AB$ and $AC$ at $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Suppose the points diametrically opposite $X$ and $Y$ both lie on the side $BC$, and let $AB = 6$. Find the area of the portion of the circle that lies inside the triangle.

positive_text: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the hyperbola $y^{2}-x^{2}=1$. Given a real number $x_{0}$, define a sequence $(x_{n})$ by letting $L_{n}$ be the line with slope 1 through $(x_{n}, 0)$, and setting $x_{n+1}$ to be the $x$-coordinate of the projection onto the $x$-axis of the intersection of $L_{n}$ with $\mathcal{C}$. If $x_{n} = 0$, the sequence ends. Let $N$ be the number of real numbers $x_{0}$ such that $x_{0} = x_{2008}$. Find $N \mod 2008$.

negatives.text: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the hyperbola $y^{2}-x^{2}=1$. Given a point $P_0$ on the $x$-axis, define a sequence $(P_n)$ where each $P_{n+1}$ is the projection onto the $x$-axis of the point of intersection of the line with slope $-1$ through $P_n$ and $\mathcal{C}$. (If $P_n = 0$, the sequence terminates.) Let $N$ be the number of such $P_0$ for which $P_0 = P_{2008}$. Find $N \mod 2008$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the hyperbola $y^{2}-x^{2}=1$. Given a point $P_0$ on the $x$-axis, define a sequence $(P_n)$ where each $P_{n+1}$ is the projection onto the $x$-axis of the point of intersection of the line with slope 1 through $P_n$ and the parabola $\mathcal{C} = y^2 - x = 1$. (If $P_n = 0$, the sequence terminates.) Let $N$ be the number of such $P_0$ for which $P_0 = P_{2008}$. Find $N \mod 2008$.

positive_text: A cyclic pentagon $PQRST$ has sides $PQ = QR = 5$, $RS = ST = 12$, and $TP = 14$. Find the radius of the circle passing through all five points.

negatives.text: Cyclic pentagon $ABCDE$ has side lengths $AB = BC = 5$, $CD = DE = 12$, and $AE = 13$. Determine the radius of its circumcircle.
Cyclic pentagon $ABCDE$ has side lengths $AB = BC = 5$, $CD = DE = 12$, and $AE = 14$. Determine the area of the pentagon.
Cyclic pentagon $ABCDE$ has side lengths $AB = BC = 5$, $CD = DE = 12$, and $AE = 14$. Determine the length of the diagonal $BD$.

positive_text: Let $a x^{2} - b x + c$ be a quadratic with distinct roots $p$ and $q$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers and $0 < p, q < 1$. Determine the smallest possible value of $a$.

negatives.text: The polynomial $a x^{2} + b x + c$ has two distinct roots $p$ and $q$, with $a$, $b$, and $c$ positive integers and with $0 < p, q < 1$. Find the minimum possible value of $a$.
The polynomial $a x^{2} - b x + c$ has two distinct roots $p$ and $q$, with $a$, $b$, and $c$ positive integers and with $0 < p < 1$ and $q > 1$. Find the minimum possible value of $a$.
The polynomial $a x^{2} - b x + c$ has two distinct roots $p$ and $q$, with $a$, $b$, and $c$ positive integers and with $0 < p, q < 1$. Find the minimum possible value of $b$.

positive_text: Determine the largest possible value of $\operatorname{Perimeter}(T)$, where $T$ is any triangle that fits inside a regular 7-gon with side length 1. Round your result to two decimal places as $N$. If the true value is $A$ when rounded to two decimal places, you receive 0 points if $N < A$; otherwise, your score is $\lfloor\max\{0, 25 - 50 \cdot (N - A)\}\rfloor$.

negatives.text: Find $\min \{\operatorname{Perimeter}(T)\}$ for $T$ a triangle contained in a regular septagon of unit edge length. Write your answer $N$ to 2 places after the decimal. If the correct answer rounded to 2 decimal places is $A$, you will receive 0 points if $N<A$ and $\lfloor\max \{0,25-50 \cdot(N-A)\}\rfloor$ points otherwise.

Find $\max \{\operatorname{Perimeter}(T)\}$ for $T$ a triangle contained in a regular septagon of unit diameter. Write your answer $N$ to 2 places after the decimal. If the correct answer rounded to 2 decimal places is $A$, you will receive 0 points if $N<A$ and $\lfloor\max \{0,25-50 \cdot(N-A)\}\rfloor$ points otherwise.

Find $\max \{\operatorname{Perimeter}(T)\}$ for $T$ a triangle contained in a regular octagon of unit edge length. Write your answer $N$ to 2 places after the decimal. If the correct answer rounded to 2 decimal places is $A$, you will receive 0 points if $N<A$ and $\lfloor\max \{0,25-50 \cdot(N-A)\}\rfloor$ points otherwise.

positive_text: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides, $n \ge 3$. A triangulation of $\mathcal{P}$ is formed by $n-3$ non-intersecting diagonals, partitioning $\mathcal{P}$ into $n-2$ triangles. Determine all integers $n$ for which such a triangulation exists where all resulting triangles are isosceles.

negatives.text: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides, $n \ge 3$. A triangulation of $\mathcal{P}$ is formed by $n-3$ diagonals that do not intersect inside the polygon. If all the triangles in the triangulation are scalene, find all values of $n$.

Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides, $n \ge 3$. A triangulation of $\mathcal{P}$ is formed by $n-3$ diagonals that do not intersect inside the polygon. If all the triangles in the triangulation are right triangles, find all values of $n$.

Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides, $n \ge 3$. A triangulation of $\mathcal{P}$ is formed by $n-3$ diagonals that do not intersect inside the polygon. If all the triangles in the triangulation are equilateral, find all values of $n$.

positive_text: Let $x, y, z, w$ be non-negative real numbers such that $x \geq y \geq z \geq w$, $x^2 + w^2 = 1$, $y^2 + z^2 = 1$, and $x z + y w = \frac{1}{3}$. Compute $x y - z w$.

negatives.text: Suppose $a, b, c, d$ are real numbers satisfying $a \geq b \geq c \geq d \geq 0$, $a^2 + d^2 = 1$, $b^2 + c^2 = 1$, and $a c - b d = \frac{1}{3}$. Find the value of $a b - c d$.
Suppose $a, b, c, d$ are real numbers satisfying $a \geq b \geq c \geq d \geq 0$, $a^2 + d^2 = 1$, $b^2 + c^2 = 1$, and $a c + b d = -\frac{1}{3}$. Find the value of $a b - c d$.
Suppose $a, b, c, d$ are real numbers satisfying $a \geq b \geq c \geq d \geq 0$, $a^2 + d^2 = 1$, $b^2 + c^2 = 1$, and $a c + b d = 1$. Find the value of $a b - c d$.

positive_text: Find all real solutions $$(a+b)^2 = (a+1)(b-1).$$

negatives.text: Find the real solution(s) to the equation $$(x+y)^2 = (x+1)(y+1).$$
Find the real solution(s) to the equation $$(x+y)^3 = (x+1)(y-1).$$
Find the real solution(s) to the equation $$(x+y)^2 = (x-1)(y+1).$$

positive_text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $S = \{1,2, \ldots, n\}$. Define a mapping $g: S \rightarrow S$ as follows:
$$
g(k)= \begin{cases}2 k & \text{ if } 2 k \leq n, \\ 2 n - 2 k + 1 & \text{ otherwise. }\end{cases}
$$
Let $g^r(k)$ denote the $r$-th iterate of $g$ at $k$. If $r$ is a positive integer such that $g^r(1) = 1$, show that $g^r(k) = k$ for all $k \in S$.

negatives.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $S = \{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Define a function $f: S \rightarrow S$ by
$$
f(x) = \begin{cases}2x & \text{if } 2x \leq n, \\ 2n - 2x - 1 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$
If $m$ is a positive integer satisfying $f^m(1) = 1$, prove that $f^m(k) = k$ for all $k \in S$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and $S = \{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Define a function $f: S \rightarrow S$ by
$$
f(x) = \begin{cases}2x & \text{if } 2x \leq n, \\ 2n - 2x + 1 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$
If $m$ is a positive integer satisfying $f^m(1) = 1$, prove that $f^m(k) = 1$ for all $k \in S$.

positive_text: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be three nonnegative real numbers such that there exist integers $p$, $q$, and $r$, not all zero, with $p x + q y + r z = 0$. In each step, choose two values $a$, $b$ with $a \le b$ and replace $b$ with $b - a$. Prove that in a finite number of steps, at least one of the numbers will become $0$.

negatives.text: Three nonnegative real numbers $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$ are written on a blackboard. These numbers have the property that there exist integers $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$, not all zero, satisfying $a_1 r_1 + a_2 r_2 + a_3 r_3 = 1$. We are permitted to perform the following operation: find two numbers $x$, $y$ on the blackboard with $x \le y$, then erase $y$ and write $y - x$ in its place. Prove that after a finite number of such operations, we can end up with at least one $0$ on the blackboard.

Three nonnegative real numbers $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$ are written on a blackboard. These numbers have the property that there exist integers $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$, not all zero, satisfying $a_1 r_1 + a_2 r_2 + a_3 r_3 = 0$. We are permitted to perform the following operation: find two numbers $x$, $y$ on the blackboard with $x < y$, then erase $y$ and write $x - y$ in its place. Prove that after a finite number of such operations, we can end up with at least one $0$ on the blackboard.

Three nonnegative real numbers $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$ are written on a blackboard. These numbers have the property that there exist integers $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$, not all zero, satisfying $a_1 r_1 + a_2 r_2 + a_3 r_3 = 0$. We are permitted to perform the following operation: find two numbers $x$, $y$ on the blackboard with $x < y$, then erase $x$ and write $y - x$ in its place. Prove that after a finite number of such operations, we can end up with at least one $0$ on the blackboard.

positive_text:
Let $x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots$ and $y_1, y_2, y_3, \dots$ be integer sequences such that
$$
(x_n - x_{n-1})(x_n - x_{n-2}) + (y_n - y_{n-1})(y_n - y_{n-2}) = 0
$$
for all $n > 2$. Prove there exists a positive integer $k$ with $x_k = x_{k+2008}$.

negatives.text:
Two sequences of integers, $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ and $b_1, b_2, b_3, \dots$, satisfy the equation
$$
(a_n - a_{n-1})(a_n - a_{n-2}) + (b_n - b_{n-1})(b_n - b_{n-2}) = 1
$$
for each integer $n$ greater than $2$. Prove that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $a_k = a_{k+2008}$.

Two sequences of integers, $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ and $b_1, b_2, b_3, \dots$, satisfy the equation
$$
(a_n - a_{n-1})(a_n - a_{n-2}) - (b_n - b_{n-1})(b_n - b_{n-2}) = 0
$$
for each integer $n$ greater than $2$. Prove that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $a_k = a_{k+2008}$.

Two sequences of integers, $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ and $b_1, b_2, b_3, \dots$, satisfy the equation
$$
(a_n - a_{n-1})(a_n - a_{n-2}) + (b_n - b_{n-1})(b_n - b_{n-2}) = 0
$$
for each integer $n$ greater than $2$. Prove that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $a_k = a_{k+2009}$.

positive_text: Let $f(x) = \cos^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + \sin^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$ for all real numbers $x$. Compute the 2008th derivative of $f$ at $x=0$, i.e., $f^{(2008)}(0)$.

negatives.text: Let $f(x) = \sin^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) - \cos^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine $f^{(2008)}(0)$.
Let $f(x) = \sin^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + \cos^6\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine $f^{(2008)}(0)$.
Let $f(x) = \sin^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + \cos^6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine $f^{(2009)}(0)$.

positive_text: Determine the total of all integers $x$ satisfying $|x + 2| \leq 10$.

negatives.text: What is the sum of all integers $x$ such that $|x+2| < 10$?
What is the sum of all integers $x$ such that $|x-2| \leq 10$?

positive_text: Suppose $f(x) = x^{3} + x + 1$. Let $g$ be a cubic polynomial with $g(0) = -1$, and let the roots of $g$ be the squares of the roots of $f$. Determine $g(9)$.

negatives.text: Let $f(x) = x^{3} - x + 1$. Suppose $g$ is a cubic polynomial such that $g(0) = -1$, and the roots of $g$ are the squares of the roots of $f$. Find $g(9)$.
Let $f(x) = x^{3} + x + 1$. Suppose $g$ is a cubic polynomial such that $g(0) = -1$, and the roots of $g$ are the cubes of the roots of $f$. Find $g(9)$.
Let $f(x) = x^{3} + x + 1$. Suppose $g$ is a cubic polynomial such that $g(0) = -1$, and the roots of $g$ are the reciprocals of the roots of $f$. Find $g(9)$.

positive_text:
Let $D$ be a point within triangle $ABC$, and define $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ as the points where the lines $AD$, $BD$, and $CD$ meet the circumcircles of triangles $BDC$, $CDA$, and $ADB$ again. Prove that
$$
\frac{AD}{AA_1} + \frac{BD}{BB_1} + \frac{CD}{CC_1} = 1
$$

negatives.text:
Let $D$ lie inside triangle $ABC$, and let $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ be the second intersection points of $AD$, $BD$, and $CD$ with the circumcircles of triangles $BDC$, $CDA$, and $ADB$. Prove that
$$
\frac{AD^2}{AA_1} + \frac{BD^2}{BB_1} + \frac{CD^2}{CC_1} = 1
$$

positive_text: Define a real number $r$ as "sparse" if the set $\{s \in \mathbb{R} \mid \exists n > 0, s^n = r\}$ is finite. Determine all such sparse real numbers.

negatives.text: A real number $r$ is said to be "sparse" if the set $\{s \in \mathbb{R} \mid \exists n > 0, s^n = r\}$ is countably infinite. Determine all such $r$.

We say "$s$ grows to $r$" if there exists some integer $n > 0$ such that $s^n = r$. Call a real number $r$ "sparse" if there are only finitely many non-negative real numbers $s$ that grow to $r$. Find all such $r$.
Define $r$ as "sparse" if there are only finitely many real numbers $s$ such that $s^n = r$ for some positive rational number $n$. Determine all sparse real numbers.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle A = 45^\circ$, and let $P$ lie on segment $BC$ such that $BP = 3$ and $PC = 5$. If $O$ is the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$, find the distance $OP$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle A = 45^\circ$. Let $P$ lie on segment $BC$ with $PB = 3$ and $PC = 5$. Let $O$ be the centroid of triangle $ABC$. Determine the length $OP$.
Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle A = 135^\circ$. Let $P$ lie on segment $BC$ with $PB = 3$ and $PC = 5$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. Determine the length $OP$.
Let triangle $ABC$ have $\angle A = 45^\circ$. Let $P$ lie on segment $BC$ with $PB = 3$ and $PC = 5$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. Determine the length $OP^2$.

positive_text:
Find all ordered pairs $(x, y)$ such that
$$
(x-2y)^2 + (1-y)^2 = 0
$$

negatives.text:
Find all ordered pairs $(x, y)$ such that
$$
(x - 2y)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 1
$$

Find all ordered pairs $(x, y)$ such that
$$
(x - 2y)^2 - (y - 1)^2 = 0
$$

Find all ordered pairs $(x, y)$ such that
$$
(x + 2y)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 0
$$

positive_text: Given that $x + \sin y = 2008$ and $x + 2008 \cos y = 2007$, where $y$ is in the first quadrant, find the value of $x + y$.

negatives.text: Given that $x + \sin y = 2008$ and $x + 2008 \cos y = 2007$, where $\pi / 2 \leq y \leq \pi$, find the value of $x + y$.

positive_text: Let $C_2$ and $C_1$ be externally tangent circles with radii $3$ and $2$, respectively. Suppose a circle $C_3$ is internally tangent to both $C_1$ and $C_2$ at points $A$ and $B$. The tangents from $T$ to $C_3$ touch it at $A$ and $B$, and the segment $TA$ has length $4$. Find the radius of $C_3$.

negatives.text: Let $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ be externally tangent circles with radius $2$ and $3$, respectively. Let $C_{3}$ be a circle internally tangent to both $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. The tangents to $C_{3}$ at $A$ and $B$ meet at $T$, and $TA = -4$. Determine the radius of $C_{3}$.

Let $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ be externally tangent circles with radius $2$ and $3$, respectively. Let $C_{3}$ be a circle externally tangent to both $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. The tangents to $C_{3}$ at $A$ and $B$ meet at $T$, and $TA = 4$. Determine the radius of $C_{3}$.

Let $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ be externally tangent circles with radius $2$ and $3$, respectively. Let $C_{3}$ be a circle internally tangent to both $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. The tangents from $T$ to $C_{3}$ touch it at $A$ and $B$, and the length $TA^2 = 4$. Determine the radius of $C_{3}$.

positive_text: A dragon named Trodgor is destroying a village made up of 90 cottages. At $t=0$, a peasant emerges from each cottage, and every 480 seconds, an additional peasant arises from every unburned cottage. Trodgor needs 5 seconds to burn either a peasant or a cottage, but he can only start burning cottages once all surrounding peasants are eliminated. What is the total time, in seconds, it takes for Trodgor to destroy all the cottages?

negatives.text: Trodgor the dragon is burning down a village with 90 cottages. At time $t=0$, an angry peasant arises from each cottage, and every 480 seconds, an additional angry peasant arises from each unburned cottage. It takes Trodgor 5 seconds to burn a peasant, but 10 seconds to burn a cottage. He can only begin burning cottages once all surrounding peasants are eliminated. How many seconds does it take Trodgor to burn down the entire village?

Trodgor the dragon is burning down a village with 90 cottages. At time $t=0$, an angry peasant arises from each cottage, and every 480 seconds, an additional angry peasant arises from each unburned cottage. It takes Trodgor 5 seconds to burn a peasant or a cottage, but he can begin burning cottages while peasants are still present. How many seconds does it take Trodgor to burn down the entire village?

Trodgor the dragon is burning down a village with 90 cottages. At time $t=0$, an angry peasant arises from each cottage, and every 480 seconds, an additional angry peasant arises from each unburned cottage. It takes Trodgor 5 seconds to burn a peasant or a cottage, but he cannot begin burning cottages until all surrounding peasants are eliminated. How many minutes does it take Trodgor to burn down the entire village?

positive_text: Find the product of all real $x$ for which $$ 2^{x} \left(2^{2x+1} - 17 \cdot 2^{x} + 8\right) = 0 $$

negatives.text: Find the product of all real $x$ for which $$ 2^{3x+1} + 17 \cdot 2^{2x} + 2^{x+3} = 0 $$
Find the product of all real $x$ for which $$ 2^{3x+1} - 17 \cdot 2^{2x} + 2^{x+3} = 1 $$
Find the product of all real $x$ for which $$ 2^{3x+1} - 17 \cdot 2^{2x} + 2^{x^2+3} = 0 $$

positive_text:
Let $x_{0} = \frac{6}{7}$, and
$$
x_{n+1} = \begin{cases}2 x_{n} & \text{ if } x_{n} < \frac{1}{2} \\

Prove that the players can be numbered $1, 2, \dots, N$ such that, whenever $a \ge b + M - 1$, player $a$ beat player $b$.

Let $N > M > 1$ be fixed integers. In a no-draws tournament with $N$ players, suppose that for any sequence of $M + 1$ players $P_0, P_1, \dots, P_M$ such that $P_{i-1}$ beat $P_i$ for each $i = 1, \dots, M$, player $P_0$ also drew with $P_M$. Prove that the players can be numbered $1, 2, \dots, N$ such that, whenever $a \ge b + M - 1$, player $a$ beat player $b$.

positive_text:
\textbf{a.} Prove that the chromatic number of a finite graph $G$ cannot decrease by more than one when a vertex and all its incident edges are deleted.

\textbf{b.} Demonstrate that, for any integer $n > 2$, there exist infinitely many graphs with chromatic number $n$ such that the chromatic number strictly decreases upon removal of any vertex.

negatives.text:
\textbf{a.} If a single vertex is removed from a finite graph, prove that the chromatic number cannot increase by more than 1.

\textbf{b.} Show that for any $n > 2$, there are infinitely many graphs with chromatic number $n$ such that removing any vertex increases the chromatic number by 1.

\textbf{a.} If a single vertex is removed from a finite graph, prove that the chromatic number cannot decrease by more than 1.

\textbf{b.} Show that for any $n > 2$, there are infinitely many graphs with chromatic number $n$ such that removing any vertex does not change the chromatic number.

\textbf{a.} If a single vertex is removed from a finite graph, prove that the chromatic number cannot decrease by more than 1.

\textbf{b.} Show that for any $n > 2$, there are infinitely many graphs with chromatic number $n$ such that removing any edge (not a vertex) decreases the chromatic number by 1.

positive_text: Given a triangle $ABC$ with lattice point vertices and side length $AB=1$, and a perimeter strictly less than $17$, determine the maximum possible value of the reciprocal of the inradius, $1/r$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle in the coordinate plane with vertices on lattice points and $AB=1$. If the perimeter of $ABC$ is greater than $17$, find the largest possible value of $1/r$, where $r$ is the inradius.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle in the coordinate plane with vertices on lattice points and with $AB=1$. Suppose the area of $ABC$ is less than $17$. Find the largest possible value of $1/r$, where $r$ is the inradius.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle in the coordinate plane with vertices on lattice points and with $AB=1$. Suppose the perimeter of $ABC$ is less than $17$. Find the smallest possible value of $1/r$, where $r$ is the inradius.

positive_text:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with angles $\angle A, \angle B$, and $\angle C$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos \angle A}{\cos (\angle B - \angle C)} + \frac{\cos \angle B}{\cos (\angle C - \angle A)} + \frac{\cos \angle C}{\cos (\angle A - \angle B)} \geq \frac{3}{2}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with angles $\alpha, \beta$, and $\gamma$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos \alpha}{\sin (\beta-\gamma)}+\frac{\cos \beta}{\sin (\gamma-\alpha)}+\frac{\cos \gamma}{\sin (\alpha-\beta)} \geq \frac{3}{2}
$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with angles $\alpha, \beta$, and $\gamma$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos \alpha}{\cos (\beta-\gamma)}+\frac{\cos \beta}{\cos (\gamma-\alpha)}+\frac{\cos \gamma}{\cos (\alpha-\beta)} < \frac{3}{2}
$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with angles $\alpha, \beta$, and $\gamma$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos \alpha}{\cos (\beta-\gamma)}+\frac{\cos \beta}{\cos (\gamma-\alpha)}+\frac{\cos \gamma}{\cos (\alpha-\beta)} = \frac{3}{2}
$$

positive_text: Let $F_{n}$ be the Fibonacci sequence, where $F_{0}=0$, $F_{1}=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_{n}$. Find the value of $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} F_{n} \cdot (\frac{1}{10})^{n}$.

negatives.text: Let $F_{n}$ be the Fibonacci sequence, where $F_{0}=0$, $F_{1}=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_{n}$. Compute $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^{n} \frac{F_{n}}{10^{n}}$.
Let $F_{n}$ be the Fibonacci sequence, where $F_{0}=0$, $F_{1}=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_{n}$. Compute $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{F_{n}}{10^{n}} + \frac{F_{n}}{10^{n+1}}$.
Let $F_{n}$ be the Fibonacci sequence, where $F_{0}=0$, $F_{1}=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_{n}$. Compute $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{F_{n}}{10^{n}} - \frac{F_{n}}{10^{n+1}}$.

positive_text: Determine the number of functions $f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \rightarrow \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ such that $f(f(x)) = f(x)$ holds for every $x$ in the domain.

negatives.text: How many functions $f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \rightarrow \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ satisfy $f(f(x)) = x$ for all $x \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$?
How many functions $f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \rightarrow \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ satisfy $f(f(x)) = f(f(f(x)))$ for all $x \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$?
How many functions $f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \rightarrow \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ satisfy $f(f(x)) \neq f(x)$ for all $x \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$?

positive_text: Let $S$ be the set of integer-coordinate points $(x, y)$ with $1 \leq x, y \leq 26$. A subset of $S$ is called convex if all its points form the vertices of a convex polygon (non-selfintersecting, with all internal angles $\leq 180^\circ$). How many such convex subsets of $S$ contain exactly 98 points?

negatives.text: A set of points is convex if the points are the vertices of a convex polygon. Let $S$ be the set of points $(x, y)$ such that $x$ and $y$ are integers and $1 \leq x, y \leq 26$. Find the number of ways to choose a non-convex subset of $S$ that contains exactly 98 points.

A set of points is convex if the points are the vertices of a convex polygon. Let $S$ be the set of points $(x, y)$ such that $x$ and $y$ are integers and $1 \leq x, y \leq 26$. Find the number of ways to choose a convex subset of $S$ that contains at most 98 points.

A set of points is convex if the points are the vertices of a convex polygon. Let $S$ be the set of points $(x, y)$ such that $x$ and $y$ are integers and $1 \leq x, y \leq 26$. Find the number of ways to choose a convex subset of $S$ that contains exactly 98 distinct points, with at least one point on the boundary of the convex hull.

positive_text: Given $x = 1000000000 - 987654321$ and $y = \frac{123456790}{10}$, find the value of $\sqrt{x y}$.

negatives.text: If $A = 10^{9} + 987654321$ and $B = \frac{123456789 + 1}{10}$, what is the value of $\sqrt{A B}$?
If $A = 10^{9} - 987654321$ and $B = \frac{123456789 + 1}{9}$, what is the value of $\sqrt{A B}$?

positive_text: Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial such that $p(x) = x^{2} + 2x + 1 + p'(x)$. Determine $p(5)$.

negatives.text: Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial such that $p(x) + p'(x) = x^{2} + 2x + 1$. Compute $p(5)$.
Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial and suppose $p(x) - p'(x) = x^2 - 2x + 1$. Compute $p(5)$.
Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial and suppose $p(x) - p'(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + 1$. Compute $p(5)$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 8$, $BC = 15$, and $AC = 17$. A random point $X$ is selected on segment $AB$, a random point $Y$ is selected on segment $BC$, and a random point $Z$ is selected on segment $CA$. Determine the expected area of triangle $XYZ$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 8$, $BC = 15$, and $AC = 17$. A point $X$ is randomly selected on segment $AB$, a point $Y$ is randomly selected on segment $BC$, and a point $Z$ is randomly selected on segment $CA$. What is the expected perimeter of triangle $XYZ$?

Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 8$, $BC = 15$, and $AC = 17$. A point $X$ is randomly selected on segment $AB$, a point $Y$ is randomly selected on segment $AC$, and a point $Z$ is randomly selected on segment $BC$. What is the expected area of triangle $XYZ$?

Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 8$, $BC = 15$, and $AC = 17$. A point $X$ is randomly selected on segment $AB$, a point $Y$ is randomly selected on segment $BC$, and a point $Z$ is fixed at vertex $C$. What is the expected area of triangle $XYZ$?

positive_text: Starting from the point $(x, y)$, you are allowed to move to $\left(\frac{x}{3}+a, \frac{y}{3}+b\right)$, where $a$ and $b$ satisfy $a^{2}+b^{2} \leq 1$. What is the area of the set of all points reachable from $(0,0)$ through a finite sequence of such moves?

negatives.text: From the point $(x, y)$, a legal move is a move to $\left(\frac{x}{3}+u, \frac{y}{3}+v\right)$, where $u$ and $v$ are real numbers such that $u^{2}+v^{2} \leq 1$. What is the perimeter of the set of points that can be reached from $(0,0)$ in a finite number of legal moves?

From the point $(x, y)$, a legal move is a move to $\left(\frac{x}{3}+u, \frac{y}{3}+v\right)$, where $u$ and $v$ are real numbers such that $u^{2}+v^{2} \leq 1$. What is the volume of the set of points that can be reached from $(0,0)$ in a finite number of legal moves?

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle in the $xy$-plane. The projections of the triangle onto the $x$-axis, $y$-axis, and the line $y = x$ yield segments with endpoints $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$, $(0,8)$ and $(0,13)$, and $(5,5)$ and $(7.5,7.5)$, respectively. Compute the area of $\triangle ABC$.

negatives.text: A triangle in the $xy$-plane is such that when projected onto the $x$-axis, $y$-axis, and the line $y = x$, the results are line segments with endpoints $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$, $(0,8)$ and $(0,13)$, and $(5,5)$ and $(7.5,7.5)$, respectively. What is the perimeter of the triangle?

A triangle in the $xy$-plane is such that when projected onto the $x$-axis, $y$-axis, and the line $y = x$, the results are line segments with endpoints $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$, $(0,8)$ and $(0,13)$, and $(5,5)$ and $(7.5,7.5)$, respectively. What is the length of the projection onto the line $y = -x$?

A triangle in the $xy$-plane is such that when projected onto the $x$-axis, $y$-axis, and the line $y = x$, the results are line segments with endpoints $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$, $(0,8)$ and $(0,13)$, and $(5,5)$ and $(7.5,7.5)$, respectively. What is the length of the longest side of the triangle?

positive_text: Let points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ be such that triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are equilateral with side length $10$. Suppose point $E$ is located in triangle $ABC$ with $EA = 8$ and $EB = 3$, and point $F$ is located in triangle $ABD$ with $FD = 8$ and $FB = 3$. Compute the area of quadrilateral $AEFD$.

negatives.text: Given distinct points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ such that triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are equilateral with side length $10$, point $E$ is located outside triangle $ABC$ with distances $EA = 8$ and $EB = 3$, and point $F$ is located inside triangle $ABD$ with $FD = 8$ and $FB = 3$. Find the area of quadrilateral $AEFD$.

Given distinct points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ such that triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are equilateral with side length $10$, point $E$ is located inside triangle $ABC$ with distances $EA = 8$ and $EB = 3$, and point $F$ is located inside triangle $ABD$ with $FD = 8$ and $FB = 3$. Find the area of triangle $AEF$ instead of quadrilateral $AEFD$.

Given distinct points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ such that triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are equilateral with side length $10$, point $E$ is located inside triangle $ABC$ with distances $EA = 8$ and $EB = 3$, and point $F$ is located inside triangle $ABD$ with $FD = 8$ and $FB = 3$. Find the area of quadrilateral $AEFD$ assuming triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are isosceles instead of equilateral.

positive_text: Determine two lines of symmetry for the curve defined by $y = x + \frac{1}{x}$. Provide your answer in the form of linear equations $y = a x + b$.

negatives.text: Find two lines of symmetry of the graph of the function $y = x - \frac{1}{x}$. Express your answer as two equations of the form $y = a x + b$.
Find two lines of symmetry of the graph of the function $y = x + \frac{1}{x^2}$. Express your answer as two equations of the form $y = a x + b$.
Find two lines of symmetry of the graph of the function $y = x + \frac{1}{x}$, but only consider lines of the form $y = a x$ (no constant term).

positive_text: Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be non-negative real numbers with $a + b + c = 1$. Find the maximum of $a + b^{2} + c^{3}$.

negatives.text: Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are non-negative real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. What is the maximum possible value of $x + y^{2} - z^{3}$?
Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are non-negative real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. What is the minimum possible value of $x + y^{2} + z^{3}$?
Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are non-negative real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. What is the maximum possible value of $x + y^{3} + z^{3}$?

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle. Define $h_{a}$ as the set of all points $P$ such that $|PB - PC| = |AC - AB|$. Define $h_{b}$ as the set of all points $P$ such that $|PC - PA| = |BA - BC|$. Define $h_{c}$ as the set of all points $P$ such that $|PA - PB| = |CB - CA|$. Determine how many points are common to $h_{a}$, $h_{b}$, and $h_{c}$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle. Let $h_{a}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PB - PC| = |AB + AC|$. Let $h_{b}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PC - PA| = |BC + BA|$. Let $h_{c}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PA - PB| = |CA + CB|$. In how many points do all of $h_{a}$, $h_{b}$, and $h_{c}$ concur?

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle. Let $h_{a}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PB - PC| = |AB - AC|^2$. Let $h_{b}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PC - PA| = |BC - BA|^2$. Let $h_{c}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PA - PB| = |CA - CB|^2$. In how many points do all of $h_{a}$, $h_{b}$, and $h_{c}$ concur?

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle. Let $h_{a}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PB - PC| < |AB - AC|$. Let $h_{b}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PC - PA| < |BC - BA|$. Let $h_{c}$ be the locus of points $P$ such that $|PA - PB| < |CA - CB|$. In how many points do all of $h_{a}$, $h_{b}$, and $h_{c}$ concur?

positive_text: You and your opponent are allocating a fixed total of 1 unit of resources to three different tasks. A task is won by the person with more resources allocated to it (you win ties). Your allocation is $\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$. If your opponent chooses their allocation uniformly at random from the set of all possible allocations (i.e., all non-negative triples summing to 1), what is the probability that you win at least two tasks?

negatives.text: You and your opponent are distributing 1 unit of effort among three tasks. Your allocation is $\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$. If your opponent chooses their allocation uniformly at random from all non-negative triples that sum to 2, what is the probability that your allocation is greater than or equal to the opponent's in at least two of the three tasks?

You and your opponent are distributing 1 unit of effort among three tasks. Your allocation is $\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$. If your opponent chooses their allocation uniformly at random from all non-negative triples that sum to 1, what is the probability that your allocation is greater than or equal to the opponent's in all three tasks?

positive_text: Let $h_{1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} x^{k}$ for all real $x$ where the series converges. For $n \geq 2$, define $h_{n}(x) = h_{1}(h_{n-1}(x))$. Find the greatest integer $r$ for which $h_{r}(x)$ is defined for some real $x$.

negatives.text: Let $g_{1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}(1 - x + x^{2} - x^{3} + \cdots)$ for all values of $x$ for which the right hand side converges. Let $g_{n}(x) = g_{1}(g_{n-1}(x))$ for all integers $n \geq 2$. What is the largest integer $r$ such that $g_{r}(x)$ is defined for some real number $x$?

Let $g_{1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}(1 + x + x^{2} + \cdots)$ for all values of $x$ for which the right hand side converges. Let $g_{n}(x) = g_{1}(g_{n-1}(x))$ for all integers $n \geq 2$. What is the smallest integer $r$ such that $g_{r}(x)$ is undefined for all real $x$?

Let $g_{1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}(1 + x + x^{2} + \cdots)$ for all values of $x$ for which the right hand side converges. Let $g_{n}(x) = g_{1}(g_{n-1}(x))$ for all integers $n \geq 2$. What is the largest integer $r$ such that $g_{r}(x)$ is defined for all real $x$?

positive_text: Let $Q(x)$ be a polynomial of degree at most $3$ satisfying $Q(x) = \frac{1}{x^2 + x + 1}$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Find $Q(5)$.

negatives.text: Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree at most $3$ such that $P(x) = -\frac{1}{1 + x + x^2}$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$. What is $P(5)$?
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree at most $3$ such that $P(x) = \frac{1}{1 + x^2 + x^4}$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$. What is $P(5)$?
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree at most $3$ such that $P(x) = \frac{1}{1 + x + x^2}$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$. What is $P(5)$?

positive_text: Let $b_{1} = 3x^{2} - x$, $b_{2} = 3x^{2} - 7x + 3$, and for $n \geq 1$, define $b_{n+2} = \frac{5}{2} b_{n+1} - b_{n}$. Determine $\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum \text{roots of } b_{n}$.

negatives.text: Let $a_{1} = 3x^{2} - x$, $a_{2} = 3x^{2} - 7x + 3$, and for $n \geq 1$, define $a_{n+2} = -\frac{5}{2} a_{n+1} - a_{n}$. As $n \to \infty$, what is the limit of the sum of the roots of $a_{n}$?
Let $a_{1} = 3x^{2} - x$, $a_{2} = 3x^{2} - 7x + 3$, and for $n \geq 1$, define $a_{n+2} = \frac{5}{2} a_{n+1} + a_{n}$. As $n \to \infty$, what is the limit of the sum of the roots of $a_{n}$?
Let $a_{1} = 3x^{2} - x$, $a_{2} = 3x^{2} - 7x + 3$, and for $n \geq 1$, define $a_{n+2} = \frac{5}{2} a_{n+1} - a_{n}$. As $n \to \infty$, what is the limit of the product of the roots of $a_{n}$?

positive_text:
Let $g(x) = -x^{2} + 10x - 20$. Determine the total sum of all $2^{2010}$ roots to the equation
$$
\underbrace{g(g(\ldots(g(x)) \ldots))}_{2010\ g\text{~s}} = 2.
$$

negatives.text:
Let $f(x) = -x^{2} + 10x - 20$. Find the sum of all $2^{2010}$ solutions to
$$
\underbrace{f(f(\ldots(f(x)) \ldots))}_{2010\ f\text{~s}} = -2.
$$

Let $f(x) = -x^{2} + 10x - 20$. Find the sum of all $2^{2010}$ solutions to
$$
\underbrace{f(f(\ldots(f(x)) \ldots))}_{2010\ f\text{~s}} = x.
$$

positive_text: In the game of Galactic Dominion, players collect cards with point values. Suppose you are playing with only two types of cards: planet cards and hegemon cards. A planet card is worth $2010$ points, and a hegemon card is worth four times the number of planet cards you hold. Starting with no cards, on each turn you take either a planet card or a hegemon card, whichever provides more points. Define a sequence $\{a_{n}\}$ where $a_{n} = 0$ if you take a planet card on turn $n$, and $a_{n} = 1$ if you take a hegemon card. Determine the smallest $N$ such that the sequence $a_{N}, a_{N+1}, \ldots$ becomes periodic (i.e., there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $a_{n+k} = a_{n}$ for all $n \geq N$).

negatives.text: In Galactic Dominion, you collect cards: planet cards worth $2010$ points and hegemon cards worth four times the number of planet cards you hold. Starting with no cards, on each turn you take the card type that gives fewer points. Let $a_{n} = 0$ if you take a planet card on turn $n$, and $a_{n} = 1$ if you take a hegemon card. What is the smallest $N$ such that $a_{N}, a_{N+1}, \ldots$ is necessarily periodic?

In Galactic Dominion, you collect cards: planet cards worth $2010$ points and hegemon cards worth four points per planet card held. Starting with no cards, on each turn you take either a planet card or a hegemon card, whichever is worth more points. Let $a_{n} = 0$ if you take a planet card on turn $n$, and $a_{n} = 1$ if you take a hegemon card. What is the smallest $N$ such that the sequence $a_{N}, a_{N+1}, \ldots$ is eventually constant (i.e., there is a value $c$ such that $a_{n} = c$ for all $n \geq N$)?

In Galactic Dominion, you collect cards: planet cards worth $2010$ points and hegemon cards worth $4$ times the number of planet cards you have. Starting with no cards, on each turn you take either a planet card or a hegemon card, whichever is worth more points. Let $a_{n} = 0$ if you take a planet card on turn $n$, and $a_{n} = 1$ if you take a hegemon card. What is the smallest $N$ such that the sequence $a_{N}, a_{N+1}, \ldots$ is strictly decreasing?

positive_text: Given 2010 positive real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2010}$ such that $x_i x_j \le i + j$ for all $i \ne j$, find the maximum possible value of the product $x_1 x_2 \cdots x_{2010}$.

negatives.text: The 2010 positive numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2010}$ satisfy the inequality $a_i a_j \ge i + j$ for all distinct indices $i, j$. Determine the largest possible value of the product $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_{2010}$.

positive_text: Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial with coefficients $\pm 1$ such that $p(x) = c_n x^n + c_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \ldots + c_0$. Suppose $r$ is a root of $p$ with $|r| > \frac{15}{8}$. What is the smallest possible degree $n$ of $p$?

negatives.text: Let $p(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \ldots + a_0$, where each $a_i$ is either $1$ or $-1$. Let $r$ be a root of $p$. If $|r| < \frac{15}{8}$, what is the minimum possible value of $n$?
Let $p(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \ldots + a_0$, where each $a_i$ is either $1$ or $-1$. Let $r$ be a root of $p$. If $|r| > 2$, what is the minimum possible value of $n$?

Let $p(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \ldots + a_0$, where each $a_i$ is either $1$ or $-1$. Let $r$ be a root of $p$. If $|r| > \frac{15}{8}$ and $r$ is an integer, what is the minimum possible value of $n$?

positive_text: How many sequences of 2010 functions $g_{1}, \ldots, g_{2010}$ from $\{0,1\}$ to $\{0,1\}$ are there such that the composition $g_{2010} \circ g_{2009} \circ \cdots \circ g_{1}$ yields a constant function? A function $h$ is constant if $h(0) = h(1)$.

negatives.text: How many ways are there to choose 2010 functions $f_{1}, \ldots, f_{2010}$ from $\{0,1\}$ to $\{0,1\}$ such that $f_{2010} \circ f_{2009} \circ \cdots \circ f_{1}$ is the identity function?
How many ways are there to choose 2010 functions $f_{1}, \ldots, f_{2010}$ from $\{0,1\}$ to $\{0,1\}$ such that $f_{2010} \circ f_{2009} \circ \cdots \circ f_{1}$ is injective?
How many ways are there to choose 2010 functions $f_{1}, \ldots, f_{2010}$ from $\{0,1\}$ to $\{0,1\}$ such that $f_{2010} \circ f_{2009} \circ \cdots \circ f_{1}$ is surjective?

positive_text: Given triangle $ABC$ with side lengths $AB=5$, $BC=7$, and $CA=8$, construct lines parallel to each side and tangent to the incircle of the triangle. These lines do not intersect the sides they are parallel to. Determine the area of the hexagon bounded by the original triangle and the three constructed lines.

negatives.text: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=5$, $BC=7$, and $CA=8$. New lines not containing but parallel to $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$ are drawn tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$. What is the area of the hexagon formed by the sides of the original triangle and the newly drawn lines?

Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=5$, $BC=7$, and $CA=8$. New lines not containing but parallel to $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$ are drawn tangent to the incircle of triangle $ABC$, but intersect the triangle sides. What is the area of the hexagon formed by the sides of the original triangle and the newly drawn lines?

Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=5$, $BC=7$, and $CA=8$. New lines not containing but perpendicular to $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$ are drawn tangent to the incircle of triangle $ABC$. What is the area of the hexagon formed by the sides of the original triangle and the newly drawn lines?

positive_text: Let $T$ be the set of numbers of the form $2^{a} 3^{b}$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers satisfying $0 \leq a, b \leq 5$. How many subsets $S$ of $T$ are closed under taking positive integer divisors?

negatives.text: Let $T$ be the set of numbers of the form $2^{a} 3^{b}$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers satisfying $0 \leq a, b \leq 5$. How many subsets $S$ of $T$ have the property that if $n$ is in $S$ then all positive integer multiples of $n$ are in $S$?

positive_text:

$$
4(x_{n-1}^{2} + x_{n}^{2}) = 10 x_{n-1} x_{n} - 9
$$
What is the greatest integer less than $x_{8}$?

negatives.text:

$$
What is the largest positive integer less than $a_{8}$?

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have points $M$ on $AC$ and $N$ on $BC$ such that $MN \parallel AB$. Let $P$ lie on $AB$ and $Q$ lie on $CB$ such that $PQ \parallel AC$. Let the incircle of triangle $CMN$ touch $AC$ at $E$ and the incircle of triangle $BPQ$ touch $AB$ at $F$. If $AE = AF$, and if $EN$ and $AB$ intersect at $R$ and $FQ$ and $AC$ intersect at $S$, prove that the incenter of triangle $AEF$ lies on the incircle of triangle $ARS$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M$ on $AC$ and $N$ on $BC$ such that $MN \parallel AB$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on $AB$ and $CB$ such that $PQ \parallel AC$. The incircle of triangle $CMN$ touches $AC$ at $E$ and the incircle of triangle $BPQ$ touches $AB$ at $F$. Suppose $AE = 2AF$, and let $EN$ intersect $AB$ at $R$, and $FQ$ intersect $AC$ at $S$. positive_text: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ be nonzero complex numbers such that $k$ satisfies both $a x^{3} + b x^{2} + c x + d = 0$ and $b x^{3} + c x^{2} + d x + a = 0$. Determine all possible values of $k$.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ be nonzero complex numbers such that $k$ is a root of both $a x^{3} + b x^{2} + c x + d = 0$ and $b x^{3} + c x^{2} + d x - a = 0$. Find all possible values of $k$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute with $\angle BAC < 45^\circ$. Let $D$ be a point inside triangle $ABC$ such that $BD = CD$ and $\angle BDC = 4 \angle BAC$. Let $E$ be the image of $C$ under reflection across line $AB$, and let $F$ be the image of $B$ under reflection across line $AC$. Prove that $AD \perp EF$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute with $\angle BAC < 45^\circ$. Let $D$ be a point inside triangle $ABC$ such that $BD = CD$ and $\angle BDC = 2 \angle BAC$. positive_text: Let $g(x) = x^{3} - x^{2}$. For a fixed constant $k$, the curves $g(x)$ and $y = k + x$ divide the plane into multiple regions. If $k$ is such that precisely two of these regions have finite area, determine the value of $k$ that minimizes the total area of those two regions.

negatives.text: Let $f(x) = x^{3} - x^{2}$. For a given value of $c$, the graph of $f(x)$, together with the graph of the line $c - x$, split the plane up into regions. Suppose that $c$ is such that exactly two of these regions have finite area. Find the value of $c$ that minimizes the sum of the areas of these two regions.

positive_text: Let $C$ be a convex region in the plane with a finite area $A$. Show that $A = 0$ if $C$ is unbounded, or $C$ is contained within a disk of finite radius.

negatives.text: Let $S$ be a convex set in the plane with a finite area $a$. Prove that either $a=0$ or $S$ is unbounded.

positive_text: Let $AB$ be a diameter of circle $O$. Let $X$ be a point on $AB$ such that $\frac{AX}{BX} = 3$. Two distinct circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are tangent to $O$ at $T_1$ and $T_2$ and tangent to $AB$ at $X$. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be the second intersections of lines $T_1 X$ and $T_2 X$ with $O$. Compute $\frac{T_1 T_2}{S_1 S_2}$.

negatives.text: AB is a diameter of circle $O$. X is a point on AB such that $AX = 3 BX$. Distinct circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are tangent to $O$ at $T_1$ and $T_2$ and to $AB$ at $X$. The lines $T_1 X$ and $T_2 X$ intersect $O$ again at $S_1$ and $S_2$. What is the ratio $\frac{T_1 T_2}{S_1 S_2}^2$?

AB is a diameter of circle $O$. X is a point on AB such that $AX = 3 BX$. Distinct circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are tangent to $O$ at $T_1$ and $T_2$ and to $AB$ at $X$. The lines $T_1 X$ and $T_2 X$ intersect $O$ again at $S_1$ and $S_2$. What is the ratio $\frac{S_1 S_2}{T_1 T_2}$?

The lines $T_1 X$ and $T_2 X$ intersect $O$ again at $S_1$ and $S_2$. What is the ratio $\frac{T_1 T_2}{S_1 S_2}$ if $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are externally tangent to $O$?

positive_text: \text{Let } a, b, c, d > 0 \text{ such that } abcd = 1. \text{ Prove that} \quad \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} + a + ab + abc}} \geq \sqrt{2}.

negatives.text: \text{Let } a, b, c, d > 0 \text{ with } abcd = 1. \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} - a - ab - abc}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} - b - bc - bcd}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} - c - cd - cda}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} - d - da - dab}} \geq \sqrt{2}.

\text{Let } a, b, c, d > 0 \text{ with } abcd = 1. \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} + a + ab + abc}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} + b + bc + bcd}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} + c + cd + cda}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2} + d + da + dab}} \leq \sqrt{2}.

positive_text: Let $a$ and $b$ be complex numbers with $a + b = 1$ and $a^{20} + b^{20} = 20$. Determine the sum of all possible values of $a^2 + b^2$.

positive_text:
Let $p$, $q$, $r$, $u$, $v$, and $w$ be complex numbers such that
$$
p = \frac{q+r}{u-2}, \quad q = \frac{r+p}{v-2}, \quad r = \frac{p+q}{w-2}.
$$
If $uv + vw + wu = 67$ and $u + v + w = 2010$, find the value of $uvw$.

negatives.text:
Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $x$, $y$, and $z$ be complex numbers such that
$$
a = \frac{b+c}{x+2}, \quad b = \frac{c+a}{y+2}, \quad c = \frac{a+b}{z+2}.
$$
If $xy + yz + zx = 67$ and $x + y + z = 2010$, find the value of $xyz$.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $x$, $y$, and $z$ be complex numbers such that
$$
a = \frac{b+c}{x-2}, \quad b = \frac{c+a}{y-2}, \quad c = \frac{a+b}{z-2}.
$$
If $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 67$ and $x + y + z = 2010$, find the value of $xyz$.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $x$, $y$, and $z$ be complex numbers such that

a = \frac{b-c}{x-2}, \quad b = \frac{c-a}{y-2}, \quad c = \frac{a-b}{z-2}.
$$
If $xy + yz + zx = 67$ and $x + y + z = 2010$, find the value of $xyz$.

positive_text: Consider a hallway bounded by the lines $x=0$ and $x=6$. Starting at the point $(3,0)$, you must travel to $(3,6)$, ensuring that your distance to $(3,6)$ is non-increasing throughout the path. Determine the area of the region that includes all possible points you can traverse during this journey.

negatives.text: You are in a hallway defined by $x=0$ and $x=6$, starting at $(3,0)$ and aiming to reach $(3,6)$. At each instant, your distance to $(3,6)$ must increase or stay the same. What is the area of the region you could traverse?

positive_text: Let $f(a, b) = a^{2} + 2a + b^{2} + 4b$. Let $(a_{1}, b_{1}), (a_{2}, b_{2}), (a_{3}, b_{3})$, and $(a_{4}, b_{4})$ be the corners of a unit square with edges aligned to the axes. negatives.text: Let $f(x, y) = x^{2} - 2x + y^{2} + 4y$. Let $(x_{1}, y_{1}), (x_{2}, y_{2}), (x_{3}, y_{3})$, and $(x_{4}, y_{4})$ be the vertices of a square with side length one and sides parallel to the coordinate axes. What is the minimum value of $f(x_{1}, y_{1}) + f(x_{2}, y_{2}) + f(x_{3}, y_{3}) + f(x_{4}, y_{4})$?

positive_text:
Let $m$, $n$ be positive integers with $m \ge n$, and let $T$ be the set of all ordered $n$-tuples $(b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n)$ of positive integers such that $b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_n = m$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{T} 1^{b_1} 2^{b_2} \cdots n^{b_n} = \sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^{n-k} \binom{n}{k} k^m.
$$

negatives.text:
Let $m$, $n$ be positive integers with $m \ge n$, and define $S$ as the set of all $n$-tuples $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ of positive integers such that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n = m$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{S} \prod_{i=1}^{n} i^{a_i} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} (-1)^{k} \binom{n}{k} k^m.
$$

Let $m$, $n$ be positive integers with $m \ge n$, and define $S$ as the set of all $n$-tuples $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ of positive integers such that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n = m$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{S} \prod_{i=1}^{n} i^{a_i} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} (-1)^{n-k} \binom{n}{k} (k+1)^m.
$$

Let $m$, $n$ be positive integers with $m \ge n$, and define $S$ as the set of all $n$-tuples $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ of positive integers such that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n = m$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{S} \prod_{i=1}^{n} i^{a_i} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} (-1)^{n-k} \binom{n}{k} k^{m-1}.
$$

positive_text: Define a function $f(x, y)$ that is linear in both variables. It satisfies $f(x, y) = \frac{1}{x y}$ for $x, y \in \{3, 4\}$. Compute $f(5,5)$.

negatives.text: A function $f(x, y)$ is linear in $x$ and in $y$. $f(x, y) = x y$ for $x, y \in \{3, 4\}$. What is $f(5,5)$?

positive_text:

$$

$$

$$

positive_text:
Let $y(t)$ be a solution to the differential equation
$$
\left(y + y'\right)^2 + y \cdot y'' = \cos t
$$
with $y(0) = y'(0) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$. Compute $y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

negatives.text:
Let $x(t)$ be a solution to the differential equation
$$

positive_text: Let $[n] = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ and denote by $S$ the symmetric group on $[n]$.  P(x) = x^{2008} + 3 x^{2007} + 6 x^{2006} + \ldots + \frac{2008 \cdot 2009}{2} x + \frac{2009 \cdot 2010}{2} 
$$
for all complex numbers $ x $. Evaluate $ P(z^2) P\left(z^{4}\right) P\left(z^{6}\right) \ldots P\left(z^{2010}\right) $.

positive_text: Suppose $$ G(x) = \frac{1}{\left(2 - x - x^{5}\right)^{2011}}, $$ and consider the power series expansion $G(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n x^n$. Determine an ordered pair of positive real numbers $(c, d)$ satisfying $$ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{b_n}{n^d} = c. $$

negatives.text: Let $$ F(x) = \frac{1}{\left(2 - x + x^{5}\right)^{2011}}, $$ and suppose $F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n x^n$ is its power series expansion. Find an ordered pair $(c, d)$ of positive real numbers such that $$ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a_n}{n^d} = c. $$

Let $$ F(x) = \frac{1}{\left(2 - x - x^{5}\right)^{2012}}, $$ and suppose $F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n x^n$ is its power series expansion. Find an ordered pair $(c, d)$ of positive real numbers such that $$ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a_n}{n^d} = c. $$

Let $$ F(x) = \frac{1}{\left(2 - x - x^{5}\right)^{2011}}, $$ and suppose $F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n x^n$ is its power series expansion. Find an ordered pair $(c, d)$ of positive real numbers such that $$ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a_n}{\log(n)^d} = c. $$

positive_text: In rectangle $ABCD$ with side lengths $AB = 3$ and $BC = 7$, let $W$ lie on $AB$ with $AW = 1$. Points $X, Y, Z$ lie on $BC, CD, DA$, respectively, such that $WXYZ$ is a rectangle with $BX < XC$. Find the value of $BX$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with $AB = 3$ and $BC = 7$. Let $W$ be a point on segment $AB$ such that $AW = 1$. Let $X, Y, Z$ be points on segments $BC, CD, DA$, respectively, such that quadrilateral $WXYZ$ is a square, and $BX < XC$. Determine the length of segment $BX$.

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with $AB = 3$ and $BC = 7$. Let $W$ be a point on segment $AB$ such that $AW = 1$. Let $X, Y, Z$ be points on segments $BC, CD, DA$, respectively, such that quadrilateral $WXYZ$ is a rectangle, and $BX > XC$. Determine the length of segment $BX$.

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with $AB = 3$ and $BC = 7$. Let $W$ be a point on segment $AB$ such that $AW = 1$. Let $X, Y, Z$ be points on segments $BC, CD, DA$, respectively, such that quadrilateral $WXYZ$ is a rectangle, and $BX < XC$. Determine the area of triangle $WXZ$.

positive_text: Find all real numbers $a$ such that the cubic polynomial $R(x) = x^{3} + a x^{2} - a x - 1$ has three distinct real roots.

negatives.text: Determine the set of all real numbers $p$ for which the polynomial $Q(x) = x^{3} + p x^{2} + p x - 1$ has three distinct real roots.
Determine the set of all real numbers $p$ for which the polynomial $Q(x) = x^{3} + p x^{2} - p x - 1$ has three real roots (not necessarily distinct).
Determine the set of all real numbers $p$ for which the polynomial $Q(x) = x^{3} + p x^{2} - p x - 1$ has three real roots, all of which are positive.

positive_text: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be complex numbers with $|x|=|y|=|z|=|x+y+z|=1$. Suppose $|x-y| = |x-z|$ and $y \neq z$. Determine the value of $|x+y||x+z|$.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers such that $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$ and $|a + b + c| = 1$. If $|a - b| = |b - c|$ and $b \neq c$, evaluate $|a + b||a + c|$.
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers such that $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$ and $|a + b + c| = 2$. If $|a - b| = |a - c|$ and $b \neq c$, evaluate $|a + b||a + c|$.
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers such that $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$ and $|a + b + c| = 1$. If $|a - b| = |\overline{a} - c|$ and $b \neq c$, evaluate $|a + b||a + c|$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with center $O$, and let $P$ be the intersection point of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of sides $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. Given $AP=1$, $BP=3$, $DP=\sqrt{3}$, and that $AC \perp BD$, compute the area of triangle $MON$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle with center $O$. Let $P$ denote the intersection of $AC$ and $BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ denote the midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$. If $AP=1$, $BP=3$, $DP=\sqrt{3}$, and $AC$ is parallel to $BD$, find the area of triangle $MON$.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle with center $O$. Let $P$ denote the intersection of $AC$ and $BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ denote the midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$. If $AP=1$, $BP=3$, $DP=\sqrt{3}$, and $AC$ is perpendicular to $BD$, find the area of triangle $MNP$.

positive_text: Determine the count of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ of mutually different integers in the range $[-31, 31]$ satisfying $x + y + z > 0$.

negatives.text: Find the number of ordered triples $(a, b, c)$ of integers such that $-31 \leq a, b, c \leq 31$, $a + b + c > 0$, and $a, b, c$ are not necessarily distinct.
Find the number of ordered triples $(a, b, c)$ of pairwise distinct integers such that $-31 \leq a, b, c \leq 31$ and $a + b + c = 0$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with side lengths $AB = 23$, $BC = 24$, and $CA = 27$. Suppose a point $D$ lies on segment $AC$ such that the incircles of triangles $BAD$ and $CBD$ are tangent to each other. Find the value of $\frac{CD}{AD}$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 23$, $BC = 24$, and $CA = 27$. Let $D$ be a point on segment $AC$ such that the incircles of triangles $BAD$ and $BCD$ are tangent and $D$ lies outside segment $AC$. Determine the ratio $\frac{CD}{DA}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 23$, $BC = 24$, and $CA = 27$. Let $D$ be a point on segment $AC$ such that the incircles of triangles $BAD$ and $BCD$ are tangent to a common external line. Determine the ratio $\frac{CD}{DA}$.

positive_text: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $3$. Let $R$ be the set of lattice points $(x, y)$ such that $0 \leq x, y \leq n$ and $|x - y| \leq 3$. Let $A_{n}$ be the number of paths from $(0, 0)$ to $(n, n)$ using only unit steps moving up or right, and entirely within $R$. Find the smallest positive real number $c$ such that $\frac{A_{n+1}}{A_{n}} < c$ for all $n$.

negatives.text: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $3$. Let $R$ be the set of lattice points $(x, y)$ such that $0 \leq x, y \leq n$ and $|x + y| \leq 3$. Let $A_{n}$ be the number of paths from $(0, 0)$ to $(n, n)$ using only up and right unit steps that stay entirely within $R$. Find the smallest positive real number $c$ such that $\frac{A_{n+1}}{A_{n}} < c$ for all $n$.

Let $n$ be an integer greater than $3$. Let $R$ be the set of lattice points $(x, y)$ such that $0 \leq x, y \leq n$ and $|x - y| < 3$. Let $A_{n}$ be the number of paths from $(0, 0)$ to $(n, n)$ using only up and right unit steps that stay entirely within $R$. Find the smallest positive real number $c$ such that $\frac{A_{n+1}}{A_{n}} < c$ for all $n$.

Let $n$ be an integer greater than $3$. Let $R$ be the set of lattice points $(x, y)$ such that $0 \leq x, y \leq n$ and $|x - y| \leq 3$. Let $A_{n}$ be the number of paths from $(0, 0)$ to $(n, n)$ using only up and right unit steps that stay entirely within $R$. Find the smallest positive real number $c$ such that $\frac{A_{n}}{A_{n+1}} < c$ for all $n$.

positive_text: Determine how many integer-coefficient polynomials $q(x)$ satisfy $\min \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\} \leq q(x) \leq \max \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\}$ for all real $x$.

negatives.text: Find the number of polynomials $p(x)$ with integer coefficients satisfying $p(x) \leq \min \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\}$ and $p(x) \geq \max \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Find the number of polynomials $p(x)$ with integer coefficients satisfying $p(x) \geq \min \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\}$ and $p(x) \leq \max \{2 x^{4}-6 x^{2}+1, 4-5 x^{2}\} - 1$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 4$, $BC = 8$, and $AC = 5$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $D$ be a point on the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $AD$ lies inside $\triangle ABC$ and $\angle BAD = \angle CAM$. If $AD$ intersects $BC$ at point $X$, find the value of $AX / AD$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 4$, $BC = 8$, and $AC = 5$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $D$ be a point on the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle BAD = 2 \angle CAM$. Let $AD$ intersect $BC$ at $X$. Compute the ratio $AX / AD$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 4$, $BC = 8$, and $AC = 5$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $D$ be a point on the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle BAD = \angle ACM$. Let $AD$ intersect $BC$ at $X$. Compute the ratio $AX / AD$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 4$, $BC = 8$, and $AC = 5$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $D$ be a point on the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle BAD = \angle CAM$. Let $AD$ intersect $BC$ at $X$. Compute the ratio $XD / AD$.

positive_text: Consider a nonconvex but not self-intersecting hexagon $ABCDEF$ where no pair of opposite sides are parallel. The internal angles satisfy $\angle A = 3\angle D$, $\angle C = 3\angle F$, and $\angle E = 3\angle B$. Moreover, the sides satisfy $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and $CD = FA$. Show that the diagonals $\overline{AD}$, $\overline{BE}$, and $\overline{CF}$ intersect at a single point.

negatives.text: In hexagon $ABCDEF$, which is nonconvex but not self-intersecting, no pair of opposite sides are parallel. The internal angles satisfy $\angle A = 2\angle D$, $\angle C = 2\angle F$, and $\angle E = 2\angle B$. Furthermore $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and $CD = FA$. Prove that diagonals $\overline{AD}$, $\overline{BE}$, and $\overline{CF}$ are concurrent.

In hexagon $ABCDEF$, which is nonconvex but not self-intersecting, no pair of opposite sides are parallel. The internal angles satisfy $\angle A = 3\angle D$, $\angle C = 3\angle F$, and $\angle E = 3\angle B$. Furthermore $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and $CD = FA$. Prove that diagonals $\overline{AD}$, $\overline{BE}$, and $\overline{CF}$ are perpendicular to each other.

positive_text: Given $P(x) = x^{4} - 29 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + c$, and the conditions $P(5) = 11$, $P(11) = 17$, and $P(17) = 23$, determine the value of $P(1)$.

negatives.text: Find the product of the coefficients of the polynomial $P(x) = x^{4} - 29 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + c$, given that $P(5) = 11$, $P(11) = 17$, and $P(17) = 23$.
Find the sum of the coefficients of the polynomial $P(x) = x^{4} + 29 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + c$, given that $P(5) = 11$, $P(11) = 17$, and $P(17) = 23$.
Find the sum of the coefficients of the polynomial $P(x) = x^{4} - 29 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + c$, given that $P(5) = 11$, $P(11) = 17$, and $P(1) = 23$.

positive_text: Let $p$ be a prime positive integer. Define a mod-$p$ recurrence of order $n$ as a sequence $\{a_k\}_{k \geq 0}$ satisfying $a_{k+n} \equiv c_{n-1} a_{k+n-1} + \cdots + c_1 a_{k+1} + c_0 a_k \pmod{p}$ for all $k \geq 0$, with $c_0, c_1, \ldots, c_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $c_0 \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. Determine the total number of such sequences of order at most $n$ in terms of $p$ and $n$.

negatives.text: Let $p$ be a prime positive integer and $n$ a non-negative integer. A mod-$p$ recurrence of degree $\leq n$ is a sequence $\{a_k\}_{k \geq 0}$ satisfying a linear recurrence relation $a_{k+n} = c_{n-1} a_{k+n-1} + \cdots + c_0 a_k$ for all $k$, where $c_i \in \{0, 1, \ldots, p-1\}$. Count the number of such sequences with $c_0 = 0$.

positive_text:
Find all real values of $a$ such that
$$
 a^{9} + \frac{9}{8} a^{6} + \frac{27}{64} a^{3} - a + \frac{219}{512} = 0
$$

negatives.text:
Find all real numbers $x$ satisfying
$$
 x^{9} + \frac{9}{8} x^{6} + \frac{27}{64} x^{3} + x + \frac{219}{512} = 0
$$

Find all real numbers $x$ satisfying
$$
 x^{9} + \frac{9}{8} x^{6} + \frac{27}{64} x^{3} - x^2 + \frac{219}{512} = 0
$$

Find all real numbers $x$ satisfying
$$
 x^{9} + \frac{9}{8} x^{6} + \frac{27}{64} x^{3} - x + \frac{219}{512} > 0
$$

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $AB = 5$, $BC = 8$, and $CA = 7$. A circle $\Gamma$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at point $A$ from the interior and tangent to side $BC$. The circle $\Gamma$ intersects sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Find the length of segment $DE$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 5$, $BC = 8$, and $CA = 7$. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle externally tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $A$ and tangent to segment $BC$. The circle $\Gamma$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Determine the length of segment $DE$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 5$, $BC = 8$, and $CA = 7$. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle internally tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $A$ and tangent to segment $AB$. The circle $\Gamma$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Determine the length of segment $DE$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = 5$, $BC = 8$, and $CA = 7$. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle internally tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at point $A$ and intersecting segment $BC$ at two distinct points. The circle $\Gamma$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Determine the length of segment $DE$.

positive_text: For every integer $n \ge 2$, let $r$ be the remainder when $2^{2n}$ is divided by $2^n - 1$. Show that $r$ is of the form $2^{2k}$ for some integer $k$, or provide a counterexample.

negatives.text: For each positive integer $n \ge 2$, consider the remainder when $2^{2n}$ is divided by $2^n + 1$. Prove that it is a power of 4, or find a counterexample.

Consider the assertion that for each positive integer $n \ge 2$, the remainder upon dividing $2^{2n - 1}$ by $2^n - 1$ is a power of 4. Either prove the assertion or find (with proof) a counterexample.
Consider the assertion that for each positive integer $n \ge 2$, the remainder upon dividing $2^{2n}$ by $2^n - 1$ is a power of 2. Either prove the assertion or find (with proof) a counterexample.

positive_text: Let $p$ be the value satisfying the following condition: if a point is selected at random from the unit square $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the probability that at least one of its coordinates is strictly greater than $p$ is equal to $p$. Determine $p$.

negatives.text: Let $p$ be the answer to this question. A point is selected uniformly at random from the square bounded by $x=0$, $x=1$, $y=0$, and $y=1$. What is the probability that at least one of its coordinates is less than $p$?

Let $p$ be the answer to this question. A point is selected uniformly at random from the square bounded by $x=0$, $x=2$, $y=0$, and $y=2$. What is the probability that at least one of its coordinates is greater than $p$?

Let $p$ be the answer to this question. A point is selected uniformly at random from the square bounded by $x=0$, $x=1$, $y=0$, and $y=1$. What is the probability that both of its coordinates are greater than $p$?

positive_text:
Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be complex numbers with $|x| = |y| = |z| = 1$. If
$$
\frac{x^{2}}{y z} + \frac{y^{2}}{z x} + \frac{z^{2}}{x y} = 1,
$$
determine the product of all possible values of $|x + y + z|$.

negatives.text:
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers with $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$. If
$$
\frac{a^{2}}{b c} + \frac{b^{2}}{c a} + \frac{c^{2}}{a b} = -1,
$$
determine the product of all possible values of $|a + b + c|$.

Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers with $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$. If
$$
\frac{a^{2}}{b c} + \frac{b^{2}}{c a} + \frac{c^{2}}{a b} = 0,
$$
determine the product of all possible values of $|a + b + c|$.

Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be complex numbers with $|a| = |b| = |c| = 1$. If
$$
\frac{a^{2}}{b c} + \frac{b^{2}}{c a} + \frac{c^{2}}{a b} = 1,
$$
determine the product of all possible values of $|a^2 + b^2 + c^2|$.

positive_text: Find the count of quadratic polynomials $Q(x) = a x^{2} + b x - c$, with $a, b, c$ as (positive) prime numbers less than $50$ (not necessarily distinct), such that $Q(x)$ has two distinct rational roots.

negatives.text: Determine the number of quadratic polynomials $P(x) = p_{1} x^{2} + p_{2} x + p_{3}$, where $p_{1}, p_{2}, p_{3}$ are (positive) prime numbers less than $50$, whose roots are distinct rational numbers.
Determine the number of quadratic polynomials $P(x) = p_{1} x^{2} + p_{2} x - p_{3}$, where $p_{1}, p_{2}, p_{3}$ are (positive) integers less than $50$, whose roots are distinct rational numbers.
Determine the number of quadratic polynomials $P(x) = p_{1} x^{2} + p_{2} x - p_{3}$, where $p_{1}, p_{2}, p_{3}$ are (positive) prime numbers less than $50$, whose roots are complex numbers.

positive_text:
Find all real values of $a$ for which
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{a-2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{a+2}+\sqrt{a}}=\frac{1}{4}
$$

negatives.text:
Find all real values of $x$ for which
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x-2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2}+\sqrt{x}}=\frac{1}{-4}
$$

Find all real values of $x$ for which
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x-2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2}+\sqrt{x}}=\frac{1}{4x}
$$

Find all real values of $x$ for which
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x-2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+2}+\sqrt{x}}=\frac{1}{4}
$$

positive_text: Let $a$ be a positive integer such that concatenating $a$ with itself results in a number $b$. If $b$ is divisible by $a^{2}$, determine the product of all possible values of $\frac{b}{a^{2}}$.

negatives.text: Rachelle picks a positive integer $a$ and writes it next to itself to obtain a new positive integer $b$. For instance, if $a=17$, then $b=1717$. She finds that $b$ is a multiple of $a$. Find the product of all the possible values of $\frac{b}{a}$.

Rachelle picks a positive integer $a$ and writes it next to itself to obtain a new positive integer $b$. For instance, if $a=17$, then $b=1717$. She finds that $b$ is a multiple of $a^{2}$. Find the product of all the possible values of $\frac{a^{2}}{b}$.

Rachelle picks a positive integer $a$ and writes it next to itself to obtain a new positive integer $b$. For instance, if $a=17$, then $b=1717$. She finds that $b$ is a multiple of $a^{2}$. Find the sum of all the possible values of $\frac{b}{a^{2}}$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 7$, and let $D$ lie on segment $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Suppose points $E$ and $F$ are on $AC$ and $BC$ such that $EF \parallel AD$ and the triangle is divided into three regions of equal area by these lines. Determine how many integer values $BC$ can take.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 7$, and let $D$ lie on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Suppose there exist points $E$ and $F$ on $AC$ and $BC$ such that $EF \perp AD$ and divide triangle $ABC$ into three parts of equal area. Determine the number of possible integral values for $BC$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 7$, and let $D$ lie on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Suppose there exist points $E$ and $F$ on $AC$ and $BC$ such that $EF \parallel AD$ and divide triangle $ABC$ into three parts of unequal area. Determine the number of possible integral values for $BC$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB = 7$, and let $D$ lie on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Suppose there exist points $E$ and $F$ on $AC$ and $BC$ such that $EF \parallel AD$ and divide triangle $ABC$ into three parts with areas in the ratio $1:2:3$. Determine the number of possible integral values for $BC$.

positive_text:
Let $c$ and $d$ be positive real numbers. Define two sequences of real numbers $\{x_{n}\}$ and $\{y_{n}\}$ for all positive integers $n$ by $(c+d i)^{n}=x_{n}+y_{n} i$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\left|x_{n+1}\right|+\left|y_{n+1}\right|}{\left|x_{n}\right|+\left|y_{n}\right|} \geq \frac{c^{2}+d^{2}}{c+d}
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

negatives.text:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive real numbers. Define two sequences of real numbers $\{a_{n}\}$ and $\{b_{n}\}$ for all positive integers $n$ by $(a+b i)^{n}=a_{n}+b_{n} i$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\left|a_{n+1}\right| - \left|b_{n+1}\right|}{\left|a_{n}\right| - \left|b_{n}\right|} \geq \frac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{a+b}
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive real numbers. Define two sequences of real numbers $\{a_{n}\}$ and $\{b_{n}\}$ for all positive integers $n$ by $(a+b i)^{n}=a_{n}+b_{n} i$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\left|a_{n+1}\right| + \left|b_{n+1}\right|}{\left|a_{n}\right| + \left|b_{n}\right|} \geq \frac{a^{2} - b^{2}}{a+b}
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive real numbers. Define two sequences of real numbers $\{a_{n}\}$ and $\{b_{n}\}$ for all positive integers $n$ by $(a+b i)^{n}=a_{n}+b_{n} i$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\left|a_{n+1}\right| + \left|b_{n+1}\right|}{\left|a_{n}\right| + \left|b_{n}\right|} \geq \frac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{a+b} + 1
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

positive_text: Let $x \diamond y = xy + x + y$ for all integers $x$ and $y$. Compute $1 \diamond (2 \diamond (3 \diamond (4 \diamond \ldots (99 \diamond 100) \ldots)))$.

negatives.text: Let $a \star b = ab + a - b$ for all integers $a$ and $b$. Evaluate $1 \star (2 \star (3 \star (4 \star \ldots (99 \star 100) \ldots)))$.
Let $a \star b = ab + a + b$ for all integers $a$ and $b$. Evaluate $(\ldots((1 \star 2) \star 3) \star 4) \star \ldots \star 100$.

positive_text: Let $A$ be a finite set of size $|A| = 225$, and let $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_{11}$ be subsets of $A$ each with $|A_i| = 45$ and pairwise intersections $|A_i \cap A_j| = 9$ for all $i \ne j$. Prove that $\left|\bigcup_{i=1}^{11} A_i\right| \ge 165$, and construct a case where equality is achieved.

negatives.text: Let $A$ be a set of 225 elements with subsets $A_1, \dots, A_{11}$, each of size 45, such that $|A_i \cap A_j| = 9$ for all $i < j$. Prove that $|A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \dots \cup A_{11}| \le 165$ and give an example achieving equality.

Let $A$ be a set with $|A| = 225$, and subsets $A_1, \dots, A_{11}$ with $|A_i| = 45$ and $|A_i \cap A_j| = 9$ for $i \ne j$. Prove that $|A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \dots \cup A_{11}| \ge 165$ and give a counterexample where equality does not hold.

Let $A$ be a set with $|A| = 225$ and subsets $A_1, \dots, A_{11}$ with $|A_i| = 45$ and $|A_i \cap A_j| = 9$ for all $i \ne j$. Prove that $|A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \dots \cup A_{11}| \ge 165$ and construct an example where the union is exactly 160.

positive_text:
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with $P(0) = 1$ and alternating nonzero coefficients of $1$ and $-1$. Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime positive integers. Prove that
$$
Q(x) = P(x^n) \cdot \frac{(x^{mn} - 1)(x - 1)}{(x^m - 1)(x^n - 1)}
$$
also has the same alternating coefficient pattern and satisfies $Q(0) = 1$.

negatives.text:
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with $P(0) = 1$ and alternating nonzero coefficients of $1$ and $-1$. Let $m$ and $n$ be relatively prime positive integers. Show that
$$
Q(x) = P(x^n) \cdot \frac{(x^{mn} + 1)(x - 1)}{(x^m - 1)(x^n - 1)}
$$
is nice as well.

holds for every positive integer $k$.

positive_text:
Fix a positive integer $n$. Two players, Phil and Ellie, play a game. Phil writes integers from 0 to $n-1$ in an $n \times n$ grid. Ellie selects a set of three squares in the shape of an L, such as: $$\text{![](attached_image_1.png)}$$ and increments each by 1 modulo $n$. Ellie wins if she can zero out the entire grid by repeating this operation. Determine who has a winning strategy when

a. $n=12$ ?

b. $n=2012$ ?

negatives.text:
Fix a positive integer $n$. Phil writes nonnegative integers less than $n$ in an $n \times n$ grid. Ellie selects an L-shaped set of three squares and adds 1 to each square. If the number $n$ appears in a square, it is replaced by 1 instead of 0. Ellie wins if she can zero out the grid using finitely many such operations. Determine who has a winning strategy when

a. $n=12$ ?

b. $n=2012$ ?

a. $n=12$ ?

positive_text: Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers with $-1 < x < y < 1$. Define $G = \frac{x}{1 - y}$ and $G' = \frac{y}{1 - x}$. If $G = G'$, determine the value of $x + y$.
